newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank -sure it won't be taken over.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank -sure it won't be taken over.

text.p: Commerzbank AG on Tuesday reaffirmed it is confident of remaining independent, in part because a surge in market capitalisation in recent years has made the bank expensive to buy.

Chief Executive Martin Kohlhaussen told the bank's annual news conference that Commerzbank's market capitalisation trebled in the last four years to reach 18.22 billion marks ($10.6 billion) on April 4.
"For that reason too, we are convinced that our successful strategy will lead us into the future in independence," Kohlhaussen said.
Kohlhaussen has on several occasions countered recurring market speculation that Commerzbank may become one of several banks to face merger or takeover bids in Germany's overcrowded banking market.
He noted that Commerzbank's share price had risen 81.2 percent between end-1992 and February 1997, beating the 59.2 percent rise in the overall banking sector share index.
